newsitem.title: HONG KONG: TVB sees '97 profit growth in low teens.
newsitem.headline: TVB sees '97 profit growth in low teens.

text.p: Television Broadcasts Ltd is likely to post profit growth in the "low teens" in 1997, said Alex Ying, TVB's general manager of corporate affairs.
"If everything is on course then I think we should have profit growth this year," Ying told Reuters in an interview, adding "we should be in the low teens, I think, at least."

The broadcasting and production company reported profit attributable to shareholders for the year ended December 31, 1996, of HK$477.2 million, a drop of 1.72 percent compared with 1995's HK$485.55 million.
An improvement in TVB's ratings and a positive outlook for consumer spending are expected to boost the company's advertising revenues, Ying said.
Confidence in Hong Kong's future after the handover will fuel consumer spending, he said.
"It's not like people do not have the money, it's just that they've been a little cautious over the last two years. But I think that spending will come back," he said.
So far this year, TVB has experienced a slight improvement in advertising revenues. "Revenues are better than last year, but there has been no dramatic turnaround," said Ying.
He said TVB's ratings "for the last 18 months have been on a tremendous uptrend", which should help boost revenues going forward.

TVB, which operates two channels in Hong Kong and claims to be the world's largest producer of Chinese-language programming, captures some 78-80 percent of the territory's television advertising revenues, Ying said.
